question: R1485 reduces ARM-host scalar/SIMD instruction work but loses SIMD format and AArch64 native throughput. Measure hardware cycles, retired instructions, branches, branch failures and front/back-end stalls to distinguish changed work from prediction and scheduling effects.
method: One ARM64 host; unchanged original mixed-ISA consumer; published baseline, byte-identical A/A, R1481 dense special plans and R1485 high-bit tagged plans. All original-image and fixed-path/inode/size/ASLR native panels retained. Hardware samples use the fixed image, 20 balanced forward/reverse cycles, minimum 20 traversals, three preflighted two-event groups.
scope: Seven predeclared case/mode pairs: scalar32 format, scalar64 format, SIMD64 format/detail, AArch64 ls raw/format and PE32 format. Raw counts and zero values remain in evidence. Unsupported events are recorded and never inferred. Whole-process counters include the unchanged setup and output work; native timing is independent.
